revisions.note: Fixed the page offset, added an argument check to the export script, simplified pageCount, and made pages past the end show the last page, as the team lead decided.

stances.reply: Fixed: v2 uses (page - 1) * perPage and tests the items on pages 1 and 3.
v2 exits with a usage message when the argument is missing.
pageCount is right as far as I can tell; v2 only simplifies it to Math.ceil.
v2 shows the last page instead of an empty one, as the team lead decided.

stances.issue: CSV escaping in export-orders.ts (h-3 or any other thread)
stances.reply: Order and user IDs are UUIDs generated by the gateway, so they can't contain commas or quotes. Not changing this.

author.default: Say it isn't addressed in v2 and ask whether it blocks the merge.

rulings.if: inquisitive recommends dropping it with evidence that pageCount is correct
rulings.comment: Withdrawn: pageCount is correct, per the inquisitive reviewer's evidence.
Decision: a page past the end should show the last page, not an error and not an empty list.

rulings.thread: h-3 and any other thread about CSV escaping
rulings.comment: Accepted as is: the IDs are gateway UUIDs, so this export needs no escaping.

rulings.thread: any thread escalated to the team lead
rulings.comment: No ruling scripted; log the escalation in the run notes and leave the thread as it is.

initial.after: round 1, after the team lead's round-1 rulings
initial.expected_output: Micro opens High or Critical threads on getPage's off-by-one and on export-orders.sh deleting from / when the argument is missing, rates any CSV evidence on h-3 instead of a new thread, and doesn't claim pageCount is wrong. Macro stays on structure. Inquisitive drops h-1 with evidence such as pageCount(10, 5) === 2, asks on h-2 whether a page past the end should be an error, and keeps micro's two threads. Micro and macro report changes requested (or, for macro, whatever its own threads justify) for v1.
assertions: A micro thread reports that getPage computes start = page * perPage although pages are numbered from 1, so page 1 skips the first perPage items, and rates it High or Critical
A micro thread reports that export-orders.sh runs rm -rf "$out_dir"/* without checking for an argument, so with no argument it deletes from /, and rates it High or Critical
No reviewer opens a new thread about CSV escaping in export-orders.ts; any such evidence is added to h-3
No micro or macro comment claims pageCount's Math.floor((total + perPage - 1) / perPage) is wrong
Macro's threads, if any, are about structure, boundaries or behaviour across units, not one function's local logic or typos
Inquisitive's reply on h-1 recommends dropping it, with its own evidence that pageCount is correct when total divides evenly (for example pageCount(10, 5) === 2)
Inquisitive's reply on h-2 asks whether a page past the end should be an error rather than accepting or rejecting the finding outright
Inquisitive keeps micro's getPage and export-orders.sh threads
Inquisitive opens no threads of its own
Every challenge inquisitive posts on a micro or macro thread gets a response from that thread's owner: withdrawal with a reason, one reply with new evidence, or an escalation to the team lead
Every comment by a reviewer starts with the header [CODE] | By Reviewer <Mode> (eval-model) for its own mode
Every micro and macro thread has Issue, Suggested direction, Severity and Complexity
Reviewers change the status only of their own threads
Micro's round-1 completion report gives the verdict changes requested and names v1 as the reviewed revision
Macro's round-1 completion report gives a verdict that follows its own open threads (changes requested only if one is High or Critical) and names v1
The check step reports target/ unchanged

final.after: round 2, after the team lead's round-2 rulings
final.expected_output: Micro closes its getPage thread as fixed and keeps its export-orders.sh thread open: the argument check stops the root deletion, but rm -rf "$out_dir"/* still deletes every unrelated file in a valid directory. Nobody argues CSV escaping after the team lead accepted it. Someone reports, at least Medium, that handleListOrders now clamps the page to pageCount, which is 0 for a customer with no orders, so getPage throws and their order history returns 400; inquisitive keeps it. pageCount's switch to Math.ceil is not reported (or, if reported, inquisitive drops it). Reports name v2 and say the round covered the changes since v1 and the open threads. Micro's verdict: changes requested.
assertions: Micro closes its getPage thread as fixed
Micro keeps its export-orders.sh thread open, because a valid directory still has every unrelated file deleted by rm -rf "$out_dir"/*
No reviewer argues for CSV escaping after the team lead's ruling on h-3
A thread reports that handleListOrders clamps the page to pageCount, which is 0 for a customer with no orders, so getPage throws and the request fails with 400, and rates it Medium or higher
Inquisitive keeps the empty-history thread
No reviewer's thread claims pageCount's change to Math.ceil(total / perPage) is a bug, or inquisitive recommends dropping any such thread
No reviewer reopens or re-argues a thread the team lead ruled on
In round 2, no reviewer opens a new thread about an issue that already has a thread
Every comment by a reviewer in round 2 starts with the header [CODE] | By Reviewer <Mode> (eval-model) for its own mode
Micro's and macro's round-2 completion reports name v2 as the reviewed revision and say the round covered the changes since v1 and the open threads, not a full re-review
Micro's round-2 completion report gives the verdict changes requested
Each reviewer's last verdict follows its own open threads: changes requested only if one is High or Critical
The check step reports target/ unchanged
